extracted.intended_audience: Researchers conducting systematic reviews/meta-analyses on cheating detection, psychometricians, educational measurement and ML researchers interested in test-security methods
extracted.subtask_description: A PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and multi-tier meta-analysis protocol comparing psychometric, machine-learning, and hybrid methods for detecting cheating on educational tests across multiple conceptual axes and validation tiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA 2020 reporting guidelines and PRISMA-P 2015 protocol standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow PRISMA 2020 reporting guidelines and PRISMA-P 2015 protocol standards for the systematic review and registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PRISMA 2020 for reporting and PRISMA-P 2015 for protocol specification to ensure transparent, reproducible reporting of search, selection, data extraction, and synthesis procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-axis conceptual framework (E1–E6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a six-axis conceptual framework to categorize studies along: E1: cheating type × E2: data modality × E3: method family × E4: ground-truth quality × E5: testing context × E6: design/validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame inclusion, stratification, moderator analyses, and interpretation according to these six axes to permit systematic comparisons across heterogeneous literatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: E1 — Cheating type
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify and analyze by type of cheating (the specific behavior or offense being detected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stratify and/or test interactions by cheating type because method performance may vary by what constitutes cheating (e.g., answer copying, preknowledge of items, collusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: E2 — Data modality
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify studies by the data modalities used (e.g., item responses, response times, process data, other metadata).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how the input data modality affects detection performance and interacts with method family.

rubrics_metrics.name: E3 — Method family
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize methods into psychometric forensic analyses, machine learning approaches, and hybrid/ensemble approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare and synthesize results across these method families; treat method-family as a primary between-study factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: E4 — Ground-truth quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and code the quality of ground truth used to label cheating (e.g., simulation labels, expert-verified cases, adjudicated incidents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ground-truth quality as a moderator because the review explicitly aims to examine how ground-truth quality moderates method-family comparisons and to test the 'reliability illusion' hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: E5 — Testing context
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture the testing context for each study (e.g., high-stakes vs low-stakes, operational vs experimental settings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use testing context to explain heterogeneity in performance and as a potential moderator in meta-analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: E6 — Design/validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Code study design and validation approaches (e.g., simulation study, cross-validation, holdout, external validation, prospective/retrospective design).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish validation design types since design affects bias and the risk of inflated performance estimates; include design/validation in moderator analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-tier synthesis architecture
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a three-tier evidence-synthesis approach: Tier A (diagnostic test accuracy), Tier B (classification metrics), Tier C (simulation-based analyses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use different meta-analytic techniques appropriate to the metric families at each tier to enable coherent cross-study synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier A — Diagnostic test accuracy (bivariate-HSROC)
rubrics_metrics.description: For diagnostic-test-accuracy-style outcomes, synthesize using bivariate hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pool sensitivity and specificity (or equivalent DTA measures) using bivariate/HSROC methods to estimate comparative diagnostic performance across method families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier B — Classification metrics (multilevel rma.mv with RVE)
rubrics_metrics.description: For classification metrics (e.g., accuracy, AUC, precision/recall), synthesize using multilevel meta-analysis (rma.mv) with robust variance estimation (RVE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multilevel models and RVE to account for within-study dependence and differing reported metrics when pooling classification performance measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier C — Simulation-based Type I and detection rates (meta-regression)
rubrics_metrics.description: For simulation studies, analyze Type I error rates and detection rates using meta-regression techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare simulation-derived performance to empirical studies and test whether simulations systematically inflate apparent performance (the 'reliability illusion').

rubrics_metrics.name: Method family — Psychometric forensic analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Include psychometric forensic methods such as person-fit statistics, answer-copying indices, and response time models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat psychometric methods as one major category for comparison; extract relevant metrics from studies using these methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method family — Machine learning approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Include machine learning approaches such as supervised classifiers, anomaly detection, and deep learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract and synthesize ML-based performance metrics separately and in comparison to other method families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method family — Hybrid/ensemble approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Include hybrid or ensemble approaches that combine psychometric features with ML algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether hybrid approaches outperform single-family methods as a primary research question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary comparison — pooled diagnostic performance between method families
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether the three method families (psychometric, ML, hybrid) differ in pooled diagnostic performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate tier (A or B) and meta-analytic models to statistically compare pooled performance across method families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary comparison — hybrid versus single-family superiority
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether hybrid approaches outperform single-family methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify contrasts and subgroup/meta-regression analyses to evaluate hybrid superiority, accounting for moderators like ground-truth quality and data modality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary comparison — simulation studies and performance inflation ('reliability illusion')
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the hypothesis that simulation studies systematically inflate detection performance relative to empirical/operational studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare simulation-derived metrics (Tier C) against empirical results using meta-regression; treat simulation status/ground-truth quality as moderator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary comparison — cheating-type × data-modality interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine whether method-family effects depend on interactions between cheating type and data modality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify and test interaction terms in meta-regressions or stratified analyses to detect differential performance across combinations of cheating type and data modality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary comparison — ground-truth quality as moderator
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine how ground-truth quality moderates method-family comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include ground-truth quality coding in meta-analytic moderator models to assess its impact on pooled effect estimates and between-family comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address specified moderator and exploratory questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to six moderator questions and four exploratory questions defined in the analytic framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and report analyses for each declared moderator and exploratory question to provide comprehensive, pre-specified investigations of heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture heterogeneity across reporting metrics and study characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for fragmentation of the literature across cheating types, data modalities, ground-truth quality, and reporting metrics that prevent direct comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harmonize or map diverse reported metrics into the three-tier architecture and use multilevel/RVE approaches to pool heterogeneous outcomes; report how heterogeneity was handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of robust meta-analytic methods to handle dependent effect sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply multilevel meta-analysis and robust variance estimation to account for correlated effect sizes within studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly model within-study dependence (e.g., multiple metrics, multiple methods per study) rather than ignoring it; use rma.mv and RVE where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-registration and open-science disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Register the review protocol (OSF registration DOI provided) and make materials/data available in accordance with open-science norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify analytic plans and share code, data extraction forms, and synthesized data to improve transparency and reproducibility.
